The evidence doesn't show that. It can't tell us why the trees were lost.

What it does show: Hansen/UMD mapped about 13.5 ha of tree-cover loss in 2025, roughly 3.9% of the 345.6 ha property. The JRC 2020 map agrees that 98% of that area was forest in 2020. The MGAP 2021 map puts about 13.1 ha of it in native forest and none in planted forest.

What it doesn't establish: the cause (clearing, harvest, fire or storm), whether land use changed to agriculture, the legality, or who was responsible. The loss data also counts any stand replacement, not just deforestation.

The finding is also still pending corroboration. 2025 is the latest year in the series, and no later year has been observed to confirm the change persists.

To test the agricultural-clearing hypothesis, you'd need 2026 data to check persistence, plus high-resolution imagery or land-cover data showing what the area became, and possibly permit records.
